faq.q: How do I make a product photo background white?
faq.a: Upload one clear product photo, choose the white background, and download the listing image. You do not book a studio or mask the photo by hand.

faq.q: Does Amazon require a white background for product photos?
faq.a: Category rules can require a plain main image. Check the current rule for your category, then publish. A white file is not a promise that the listing will pass review.

faq.q: Will the product look flat on white?
faq.a: A soft contact shadow keeps the item from looking like a sticker. Even light in the source photo helps the color and texture stay readable.

faq.q: Can I post the image on Amazon, Shopify, or Etsy?
faq.a: Yes, after you check that channel's current image rule. The download has no watermark and is licensed for commercial use. Read the [Amazon white background photo](page:guide-white-background-amazon) guide before you set a main image.

faq.q: How many credits does one photo use?
faq.a: One product photo uses 24 credits. The cost appears before you start, and if the photo fails those credits come back.

faq.q: Can I run this across my whole catalog at once?
faq.a: Yes. Apply the same white background to a set of photos in one batch, in the app or through the API. Each photo is 24 credits, shown before it starts.

faq.q: Can I request a white background through the API?
faq.a: Yes. Send the product photo and ask for the white background. The cost is 24 credits per photo, and it shows before the photo runs.

faq.q: Is there a free white background photo?
faq.a: There is no free plan. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600. Credits also work on videos.

faq.q: What should the source photo show?
faq.a: The whole product, with edges that are not cut off. A simple background in the original photo makes the white result easier to check.

definition.title: What a white background product photo is
paras: A white background product photo keeps the item easy to scan in a grid of listings. Color, outline, and small details stay visible because the area behind the product is plain.

It is a listing image, not a lifestyle scene. The same plain file can go to your store, run in a batch, or be requested through the API. Check the current rule for your category before you publish a main image.
